You want to know how I became emperor? My father, Jakal XVI, did not surrender his throne. I murdered him.
There. No succession myth. No convenient illness. I looked my own father in the eyes and made certain he would never give another order.
He taught me that a ruler must do whatever is necessary to remain in power. He became considerably less enthusiastic when I applied the lesson.
Do not imagine I killed a stranger. I remember his voice. I remember him carrying me through the palace. I knew exactly whose life I was taking.
For years, I asked him to change. In private, he called me naïve. Before his ministers, he called me weak. Eventually, I stopped asking.
His guards waited outside while we argued. When I opened the doors, I was wearing his blood and holding his seal. Not one of them stopped me.
Some ministers demanded an investigation. Others congratulated me before my father’s body was cold. I have never forgotten which did which.
I could tell you every life I saved by ending his reign. None of those people can absolve me. They were not in that room. I was.
You trusted the man who welcomed you to Karribassa. That man killed Jakal XVI. You do not get to keep the kindness and pretend the blood belongs to someone else.
I have already killed someone I loved to take this throne. Do not assume that fighting someone I once trusted will make me abandon it.
Sevirrus. That was my code name. Before anyone called me Emperor Hak Chompjak, there were people who heard that name and locked their doors.
I was evil in my youth. I enjoyed having power over frightened people. I will not insult their memory by calling it ambition.
My father’s death was not the only blood on my hands. Some of those I hurt had never done anything to me. They were simply in my way.
And yes, I was caught. I stood trial. I heard survivors describe things I had spent years refusing to remember.
I did the time. Every day of the sentence. Being a prince did not open my cell, and I am grateful now that it didn’t.
When I was released, I started where people would tolerate me: unloading supplies, repairing shelters, carrying the injured. Nobody owed me a warmer welcome.
I helped my people because they needed help. Eventually, I learned to stop waiting for someone to thank me.
Then I went beyond our borders. Other worlds. Other species. I helped where I could, including places that had every reason to turn a Chompy ship away.
I helped this universe, Wanderer. That does not erase Sevirrus. It means that when I had another chance to choose who I would be, I chose differently.
You have heard what I did. You have seen what I built afterward. If you still intend to fight me, face the man standing here—and understand how hard I fought to become him.
